card.name: Words right before intent or intention
card.fires_on: The word just before a form of intent, intention or intended, where the next word is predictable. Seen in legal and political text about what authors or lawmakers meant, and in phrases like well-intentioned.

modes.label: Legal meaning
modes.description: Words before intent in talk of what the framers or parties meant.
modes.example: the court must interpret the condition in light of the parties<<'>> intent.

modes.label: Adjective before intentions
modes.description: A describing word that leads into intentions, such as well- or bad.
modes.example: many<< well>>-intentioned reform efforts have been unsuccessful

modes.label: Intended in a table
modes.description: The start of the word Intended in a column heading.
modes.example: Original<< Int>>ended Dosage Adjusted Dose At
